A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. Renamings and relocations can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama-2 and Mistral experiments, benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results, including benchmark evaluations, ablations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: DR-ICL is renamed DrICL. Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same differentiated objective, PCW masking, importance sampling, exponential advantage weights, and training procedure.

E1.justification: MICLB is renamed ICL-50, but its constituent datasets and seven task categories remain unchanged. The same benchmark evaluations and WinoWhy ablation coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain NFT, IT, and MetaICL, with MetaICL remaining the comparator in the cMedQA ranking table. Newly cited IAD is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same base models, metrics, hyperparameters, and evaluation procedures. Appendices A.3 and B.1 preserve the sampling instructions, shot grid, reported evaluation sample counts, and whole-test-set checks.

E4.justification: The WinoWhy component/window ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, performance-variance analysis, and training-loss sensitivity analysis are retained. Moving the variance analysis into the main text adds no experiment; the new limitations describe future investigations.

E5.justification: The same variances across shot counts and training progress are reported. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and v3 adds no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All 11 matched tables retain their data. Main results, ablations, whole-test-set scores, and variance values are unchanged after renumbering; the figures also retain the same plotted results.

T1.justification: The loss definitions, window formulas, importance-weight ratio, reward, and exponential advantage equations remain unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same causes of many-shot degradation, differentiated/reweighting contributions, benchmark contribution, and improved in-domain and out-of-domain performance. Renaming and abstract editing do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds specific limitations absent from v1: robustness across dataset scales is insufficiently analyzed, and fixed windows may oversample short-text tasks and undersample long-text tasks. Dynamic windows are proposed as future work.

D1.justification: The release footnote changes the repository path from xiaoqzhwhu/DR-ICL to xiaoqzhwhu/DrICL. Implementation settings, hardware information, and data preparation instructions remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a change in the released artifacts.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds IAD, Liu et al. (2024b), to the instruction-tuning discussion and bibliography. The remaining related-work coverage and research positioning are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 renames the method and benchmark, locally revises the abstract, introduction, and importance-sampling explanation, and updates authorship and affiliations. It adds acknowledgments and limitations and consolidates the appendix variance discussion into Section 4.3.2.

P2.justification: The appendix variance table moves from v1 Table 10 to v3 Table 7 in the main text. Several figures are enlarged, method labels updated, and tables and Algorithm 1 repositioned; all eight figures and eleven tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency by explicitly acknowledging untested dataset-scale robustness and possible sampling imbalance from fixed windows, qualifications absent from v1. Larger plots and placing variance evidence beside its main discussion also help readers. The method and empirical evidence remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
